title: Nadeem v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. & Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of without deciding merits; petitioner to file a representation within three weeks for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks of receipt; no coercive action on the citation dated 18.11.2020 for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; no benefit if the representation is not filed
headnote: A provisional assessment under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 does not become a final assessment merely because the consumer filed no objection, including failure to reply within 15 days. Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in a theft case. Applying Shishir Jain, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount unless a final assessment is made after an opportunity of hearing and a copy of that order is supplied. Treating the provisional figure as final without a hearing is dehors Section 126 and Clause 8.1 and violates natural justice. Without entering the merits, the Court directed a representation for a speaking final assessment after hearing and stayed coercive action on the 18 November 2020 recovery citation; it did not quash the citation.
facts: Nadeem filed Writ-C No. 27089 of 2020 in the Allahabad High Court seeking certiorari to quash a recovery citation dated 18 November 2020 issued by respondent no. 4, and a mandamus restraining recovery of Rs. 1,68,364. He said he held a valid electricity connection and paid bills regularly. On 11 September 2019 a checking squad inspected his premises and reported theft of electricity. An FIR was lodged on 25 September 2019 under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003. A provisional assessment notice dated 31 October 2019 under Section 126 was sent to him by registered post. He did not file an objection. He alleged that no final assessment notice was thereafter served, yet the citation issued, and that Section 126(3) of the Act and Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had not been followed. Counsel for the Power Corporation (respondent nos. 2 and 3) could not show that want of a reply within 15 days converts the provisional assessment into a final assessment.

reusable_constructions.construction: Want of objection to a provisional assessment, including failure to reply within 15 days, does not convert it into a final assessment.
A consumer cannot be compelled to deposit on a provisional assessment unless a final assessment is made after an opportunity of hearing and a copy of that order is supplied.

Treating the amount in a provisional assessment as the final assessment without a hearing is dehors Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005, and violates natural justice.
Clause 8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005 is the licensee's procedure for inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in a case of theft of electricity.

holding_units.topic: theft assessment — provisional figure cannot be treated as final without hearing
holding_units.question: May a licensee recover a theft demand by treating a Section 126 provisional assessment as final because the consumer filed no objection within 15 days, without a hearing and without supplying a copy of a final order?
holding_units.holding: No. The Court was not convinced that absence of objection to a provisional assessment treats it as final. Clause 8.1, read with Section 126, requires inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and a final assessment in theft cases. Treating the provisional amount as the final assessment without a hearing, and compelling deposit without supplying a copy of that order, is dehors Section 126 and Clause 8.1 and violates natural justice. Applying Shishir Jain paragraph 16, the petitioner could not be compelled to deposit on the provisional figure. Without deciding merits, he was directed to file a representation within three weeks for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks of receipt. Coercive action on the 18.11.2020 citation is stayed for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; if he does not file the representation, he gets no benefit of the order.
holding_units.qualifier: The citation was not quashed. Petitioner invoked Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1; the Court's holding is framed as Section 126 and Clause 8.1.

holding_units.topic: no compulsion to deposit a provisional Section 126 assessment until a final assessment after hearing
holding_units.question: Does failure to object to a provisional Section 126 assessment, including within 15 days, convert it into a recoverable final assessment?
holding_units.holding: No. Licensee's counsel could not show that want of a reply within 15 days treats the provisional assessment as final. Following Shishir Jain paragraph 16, without a final assessment after considering the objection and giving an opportunity of hearing, and without supplying a copy of that order, the petitioner cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount. The procedure adopted was held dehors Section 126. Recovery was not allowed to proceed as a concluded final assessment; it was stayed pending a speaking decision on a representation after hearing.
holding_units.qualifier: Petitioner invoked Section 126(3); the Court's own holding is framed as Section 126. The citation was not quashed.

principle_tags.application: A provisional notice dated 31.10.2019 was served by registered post. No objection was filed and no final assessment was served. The Court would not treat the provisional figure as final, or permit recovery on it, without an opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: Clause 8.1 was applied as the theft path requiring inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment; treating the 31.10.2019 provisional figure as final without hearing was held to violate that procedure and natural justice.

principle_tags.application: An FIR under Section 135 did not displace the Section 126 / Clause 8.1 assessment procedure; the Court still required a hearing and a final assessment before recovery of the theft demand.
